attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack essay, stated as his assertion. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The performance-gap part is stated firmly ('we know'), so it is an observation. The robustness part is a tentative inference, and the drafter's 'suggesting' keeps that hedge. Identifying the system as GPT-4o image generation fits the context, which names ChatGPT 4o.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: success on publicized prompts does not carry over reliably to comparable fresh prompts. Requiring comparable difficulty is a reasonable reading of a claimed gap. Marcus gave no metric or threshold, so the result depends on this reading.

evidence.note: Alexander's dated report shows the five publicized prompts succeeding in June 2025. This supports only the familiar-prompt success part. His separate failure example is more complex, so it does not show a gap on comparable fresh prompts.
An independent preprint documents GPT-4o failures in complex scenes. It does not compare publicized prompts with comparable fresh ones, so it cannot establish or refute the gap.

An independent study reports strong compositional abilities alongside some limitations. This cuts against a broad lack of robustness, but it does not measure performance on familiar versus fresh prompts.

reviews.rationale: Only the claim that GPT-4o succeeds on the publicized prompts is supported (e1). The central claim, a recurring performance drop on comparable prompts that had not been publicly discussed, has no comparative testing in the packet. The two research papers report both strengths and failures, but neither separates prompt novelty from difficulty. The packet therefore does not settle the claim either way.
